newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures lower as doubts enter market.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures lower as doubts enter market.

text.p: Bund futures spent much of Monday drifting narrowly at lower levels with traders growing nervous about the market's ability to continue posting strong gains.

Traders said they saw a risk that the market could pull back further from its 103.74 high of February 18 and that they are nervous about west German state consumer price reports which should be released starting Tuesday.
At 1500 GMT, the March Bund future was down 20 basis points at 103.23 -- a level that it had rested near much of the day after dropping shortly after the open.
Traders said the market's main focus is Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony starting Wednesday.
Some fear he will comment on the chances for higher U.S. inflation -- remarks which would could send Treasuries lower and pull Bunds down.
Closer to home, state CPI reports pose the clearest threat, but the market is also closely watching a "tax summit" in Bonn between the ruling coalition and opposition SPD party.
No major announcements are likely to emerge from the gathering, however, as both sides are seen holding sharply different views and in no mood to quickly compromise.
Bunds continued to hold a weak tone compared to Treasuries with the spread at 92 basis points, down two basis points from the previous close.

Traders said it was hard to put a technical support point on the future contract because it had risen so steeply recently, but that today's low of 103.18 could limit any further declines on Wednesday.

A pair of economic indicators today had little impact on the market. German January producer prices rose 0.3 percent from the month before and the Bundesbank revised December manufacturing orders to -1.8 percent from -1.4 percent.
